messages.content: You are a computer science tutor. Answer clearly and accurately in at most 150 words.
Explain why a queue is useful for handling incoming print jobs. Give one concrete example and one limitation.

runs.output_text:
A queue is ideal for print jobs because it enforces First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering, ensuring fairness and preventing starvation. Printers are single-resource devices; without a queue, concurrent requests would cause data corruption or lost jobs. The queue buffers requests, allowing the printer to process them sequentially at its own pace.

**Concrete Example:** In an office, if Alice and Bob both send documents to the network printer simultaneously, the queue ensures Alice’s job (submitted first) prints completely before Bob’s begins, preventing mixed pages.

**Limitation:** A standard queue lacks priority handling. If a critical, urgent document arrives after a massive 100-page report, it must wait for the entire report to finish. This "head-of-line blocking" can cause unacceptable delays for time-sensitive tasks, requiring a priority queue instead.

A queue is ideal for print jobs because it enforces First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering, ensuring fairness and preventing race conditions when multiple users send documents simultaneously. This structure decouples job submission from execution, allowing the printer to process tasks sequentially without losing requests.

**Concrete Example:** In an office, if User A submits a 50-page report and User B submits a 1-page memo, the queue ensures User A’s job prints first. Without a queue, the printer might interleave pages or prioritize the smaller job arbitrarily, causing confusion and potential data loss.

**Limitation:** A standard queue lacks priority handling. If an urgent, one-page contract arrives after a massive, low-priority batch job, it must wait until the entire batch finishes. This can cause unacceptable delays for critical tasks, requiring a priority queue instead.

A queue is ideal for print jobs because it enforces First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering, ensuring fairness and preventing race conditions when multiple users send documents simultaneously. This structure decouples job submission from execution, allowing the printer to process tasks sequentially without overwhelming the system.

**Concrete Example:** In an office, if User A submits a 50-page report and User B submits a 1-page memo, the queue ensures User A’s job starts first. The printer processes pages in the exact order received, maintaining predictable service levels.

**Limitation:** Standard queues lack priority handling. If a critical, urgent document arrives after a long queue of low-priority tasks, it must wait until all preceding jobs finish. This can cause unacceptable delays for time-sensitive materials, requiring more complex priority queues instead.

A queue is ideal for print jobs because it enforces First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering, ensuring fairness and preventing race conditions when multiple users send documents simultaneously. This structure decouples job submission from execution, allowing the printer to process tasks sequentially without losing requests.

**Concrete Example:** In an office, if User A submits a 50-page report and User B submits a 1-page memo, the queue ensures User A’s job starts first. The printer processes the entire report before beginning the memo, maintaining predictable order.

**Limitation:** Standard queues lack priority handling. If a critical, urgent document arrives after a long queue of low-priority tasks, it must wait until all preceding jobs finish. This can cause unacceptable delays for time-sensitive materials, requiring a priority queue instead.
